title: Install forensics: telemetry gap and runbook updates
content:
Meeting: Install Forensics + Runbook Update (ad-hoc)
Dates: notes taken 2026-04-08, follow-ups 2026-04-09..10
Attendees: Elena Park (owner), Samir Gupta (SRE), Lina Chen (Field Eng), Ben Torres (Infra), Priya Iyer (Solutions Eng)
Purpose: Triage recent customer on-prem install failures seen across two customers in the past 72h. Primary goals: (1) establish short-term mitigation to keep customer instances healthy, (2) root-cause the telemetry blind spots that prevented early detection, (3) update runbook and installer checks to prevent recurrence.

High-level summary:
- Two separate installs (Customer A: EU-regulated telco, Customer B: mid-market analytics) failed during post-install validation. Symptoms similar: agent service repeatedly entering CrashLoopBackOff after first model pull (~30–90s after start). On A we saw kernel OOM kills, on B a segfault in the native quantization library.
- Root cause appears to be a combination of (a) driver/runtime mismatch (NVIDIA driver vs CUDA/cuDNN expected by model runtime) and (b) missing early-detection telemetry in the installer: the installer validated Docker/container runtime but did not validate GPU module ABI compatibility nor capture coredumps before the agent restarts.
- Short-term mitigations applied to both customers and rollout patch planned for installer and runbook.

Detailed timeline and notes:
- 2026-04-06 21:14 UTC: Customer A install begun via agentless workflow. Installer reported success, cluster registered, but within 45s the inference-agent pod crashed repeatedly.
  - Logs: repeated SIGKILL with message 'OOM killed' in systemd journal. Kernel oom_score_adj showed the agent had very high RSS allocation before crash.
  - Infra note: machine had Ubuntu 22.04 with NVIDIA driver 520.x but CUDA 12.x libraries that are incompatible with compiled runtime.
- 2026-04-07 01:02 UTC: Customer B install (on-prem bare-metal) reported immediate segfault in libredwood_quant.so during model load. Crash produced no coredump (coredump disabled on host). Installer mark 'healthy' because readiness probe only checked process existence, not successful model load.

Investigation hypotheses and evidence:
- Hypothesis 1: GPU driver mismatch triggers fallback paths in runtime that allocate unexpectedly large pinned memory -> OOM on smaller machines. Evidence: driver mismatch noted on Customer A; reproducer on CI using driver 520 + runtime compile options triggered high RSS in same codepath.
- Hypothesis 2: Native quant lib built against glibc ABI not present on older systems -> immediate segfault. Evidence: Customer B hosts run Debian 10 derivative; symbols in segfault trace point to unresolved symbol in quant lib.
- Hypothesis 3: Installer lacks early telemetry for these specific failures (no kernel logs/coredumps captured, and readiness check too coarse). Evidence: both incidents had insufficient logs to debug until field engineer ran manual systemd/journalctl and enabled coredumps.

Short-term mitigations (what we did):
- Rolled patch v0.9.7-hotfix to installer to perform additional preflight checks: detect NVIDIA driver version + run nvcc --version if present; verify kernel module presence (nvidia-smi output). This hotfix was shipped to both customers and flagged in the console.
- Added a post-install sidecar to fetch kernel logs and attempt to enable coredump collection (systemd-coredump or ulimit -c) for 24h to capture possible segfaults.
- For Customer A we increased memory limit on agent pod to 20Gi temporarily to avoid OOM while we reproduced locally. Not ideal but buys time.
- For Customer B we provided a static build of the quant lib compiled with older glibc compatibility flags and staged it via S3; field engineer swapped the library and agent recovered.

Telemetry gaps identified (actionable list):
1) Installer health check is process-existence only (k8s readinessProbe exec returns 0). Needs to be replaced with a 2-step probe: (a) process alive, (b) model load smoke-test returning expected token from the model.
2) No automatic collection of kernel logs / dmesg at time of crash. Add optional telemetry upload for kernel logs within first 5 min of agent crash.
3) Coredumps disabled by default on hosts; installer should attempt to enable temporary coredump capture or at least archive /var/log/syslog/journal on failure.
4) GPU ABI compatibility check missing. Add check for nvidia-smi + driver CUDA compatibility matrix and fail fast with explicit actionable message to customer.

Runbook update proposals (short):
- Preflight checks (new):
  * verify OS baseline (Ubuntu 20.04/22.04, RHEL8+), glibc version >= x.y or auto-compat mode
  * if GPU present: run nvidia-smi, capture driver version, verify driver >= 525 for CUDA 12 support (table attached in runbook)
  * verify kernel cgroup config and cgroupv2 interactions (notes for hosts with systemd + cgroupv2)
  * check for ulimit -c, systemd-coredump active; if not present, optionally enable for 24h and record how to revert
- Post-install probes (new):
  * model-smoke probe: attempt to load a tiny verification model (or run a quick forward pass) on the same runtime path used for production models; fail install with clear error and remediation steps if load fails
  * logs-upload trigger: on crash or repeated restart, capture journalctl -k -u inference-agent -b and dmesg output and upload to secure diagnostics bucket (customer opt-in)
- Customer communication template changes: add a single-page 'Common GPU install errors' to attach on failure that lists driver mismatch messages and how to remediate.

Longer-term engineering work (prioritized):
- Priority P0 (this sprint): implement model-smoke probe and ABI compatibility checks into installer core.
- Priority P1: automated coredump enable/disable toggle + secure ephemeral upload to diagnostics.
- Priority P1: extend console to surface preflight GPU compatibility with hyperlinks to driver download pages for clouds/vendors.
- Priority P2: provide a precompiled portable quant lib bundle for older glibc hosts; automate fallback selection during agent bootstrap.
- Priority P3: instrument runtime to expose memory allocation site metrics (KV cache, pinned memory) into our telemetry pipeline so we can set SLOs/alerts for abnormal allocations.

Open tickets and owners:
- PD-4127: Installer preflight: GPU ABI check and driver matrix (Owner: Samir)
- PD-4132: Add model-smoke readiness probe and test harness (Owner: Lina)
- PD-4135: Temporary coredump enablement + telemetry upload (Owner: Ben)
- PD-4140: Portable quant lib packaging and smoke-test (Owner: Priya)

Customer impact notes (to include in CS/Success comms):
- Customer A: brief downtime during patching window; no data loss, model queries returned 503 for ~12 minutes while we increase memory and redeploy. CS already issued incident summary and next steps.
- Customer B: agent recovered after library swap; we plan to push the safer fallback in 0.9.8 to prevent manual patching in future.

Unresolved questions / notes to follow up:
- Should installer always enable coredumps for the first 24h after install by default? Security/privacy implications — need legal/infosec input. (Action: Elena to loop in Security)
- How to maintain a portable set of quant libs safely without exploding artifact matrix? Consider compressing by glibc buckets (Action: Priya to propose packaging scheme).
- Do we want model-smoke probe to pull from customer model store or use a standardized tiny verification model? Practicality: customer privacy may block model pulls. (Action: Lina to surface options and preference data)

Immediate next steps (next 72h):
- Samir: land PD-4127 draft with driver matrix and implement quick NV check in installer (ETA 2026-04-10).
- Lina: implement minimal model-smoke PoC in private-installer repo and run against QA cluster (ETA 2026-04-11).
- Ben: implement temp coredump toggle and test on internal bare-metal; ensure logs upload uses encrypted S3 and access RBAC (ETA 2026-04-12).
- Priya: prepare portable-quant packaging plan and a customer-facing playbook for B until 0.9.8 (ETA 2026-04-13).
- Elena: draft customer comms for both customers that explain root cause, mitigation, and timeline; loop in Legal/Security on coredump proposal (ETA 2026-04-10).

Notes to self (informal):
- Quick reproducer: spin up Ubuntu 22.04 VM with nvidia driver 520 and runtime built against CUDA 12 and run the model load smoke harness — I hit the OOM locally when pinned memory went crazy. Add instrumentation to locate exact allocation call.
- Keep an eye on PD-4099 (installer telemetry refactor) — may overlap so coordinate.

Appendix: helpful log snippets (sanitized)
- Customer A (journal): "kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 1243 (inference-agent) score 123 or sacrifice child"
- Customer B (stderr): "segfault at 0 ip 0x7f6a2b8f1234 sp 0x7ffcfdcba000 error 4 in libredwood_quant.so[7f6a2b800000+26000]"

End notes: focus this sprint on fast automatic fail-fast checks (driver/ABI) + a small smoke probe; those two will buy us the biggest reduction in time-to-detection and reduce manual field work substantially.

-- Elena
